findings.description: validateCell uses board[choice - 1] for human but board[choice] for bot.
Passing string board[] decays to a pointer with no size information.
In the bot branch: if (board[choice] == player.symbol || board[choice] == "X") fails when bot is 'X' and the cell has 'O'.
The bot keeps picking random (row, col) until it finds a free cell. If the board is full, it loops forever.
Player symbol is printed directly. If provided from untrusted input, it could include escape sequences.
Long or unexpected symbols can corrupt the board state that relies on string comparison with "X"/"O".
Stream/EoF handling can cause a tight loop on EOF.
